newsitem.title: UK: Euro products outlook - refiner margins may shrink.
newsitem.headline: Euro products outlook - refiner margins may shrink.

text.p: European oil products look set for a bumpy ride this week, said oil traders.
The underlying price trend is likely to be broadly neutral but some believe the spread between gasoline and fuel oil will narrow, possibly hitting refinery margins.

Gasoline prices were expected to be volatile as traders balanced arbitrage opportunities to the U.S. and buying ahead of the U.K. budget on November 26, with signs that the European market was well supplied.
Heavy buying into the Thames ahead of the budget has widened the backwardation to early December prices.
Traders cautioned that any softening in that support could quickly lead to lower prices.
"Prices from a demand and supply perspective are far too high," said one trader in Germany. "The consumer is well supplied."
He said premium unleaded barges were fairly valued at $200 fob ARA and regular at $190, well below current levels near $230 and $220, respectively.
Mediterranean gasoline was expected to fall with ample supply of lower octane grades and demand satisfied this month. "I think early next week values may drop," said a trader.
He expected about a $3-$4 selloff. Arbitrage to the U.S., Colombia and possibly west Africa has opened, he said.

Naphtha was expected to fall based on its own fundamentals, but most action hinged on crude oil prices and buying in the swaps. One trader expected NWE cargoes to hold between $220 and $225 cif, down about $5 from last week.

In gas oil, 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil premiums focus on whether the dominant long in last week's big Nov IPE futures expiry finds takers in NWE by the end of the month - depressing premiums -- or finds homes for the bulk of it outside the region or in its own network -- supporting values at current levels.

The trader with most of the record high 865,100 tonne delivery indicated it had no need to sell into the ARA barge market and was confident it had homes in its downstream German and French networks and in Asia.

"If they keep to that position, the second half November barges will stabilise around $4.50 or $5 (their current level)," one trader said. "If they let material go (to ARA), the whole play is blown to smithereens."
One trader predicted that if the weather remained mild the company could go long Dec-Jan and Jan-Feb, selecting a colder month on which to exert pressure.
Low sulphur cracked fuel looks set to hold onto last week's gains. Stronger U.S premiums resulting from colder weather and more expensive gas will bolster European prices.
"I think we can go past $140 cif Med," commented a dealer.
High sulphur cracked fuel looks balanced but utilities in the north will probably continue to spurn material at current prices.
A rumoured Russian fuel levy for failed to materialise on Friday so uncertainty will continue this week.
